clue.text: Student from Arab country in conflict returned Justinian's code

indicators.note: the student and the country are placed inside the word for fighting
something returned goes back the way it came, so the word for fighting is read from right to left

parts.note: a war is an armed conflict
Oman is a state on the Arabian peninsula
L for learner, the plate a student driver displays

explanation.surface: A foreign student hurries home from a war-torn Gulf state, clutching a textbook on Justinian.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the word for conflict turns round, giving RAW, which then wraps OMAN and L to make ROMAN LAW.
explanation.definitionFit: The Byzantine emperor Justinian codified the legal system of ancient Rome, so his code is the classic statement of it.

clue.text: Stock in trade

parts.note: surface reading: the goods a business routinely keeps and sells
setter's reading: soup stock, sold in the shops under a trade name

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'stock in trade' means a business's usual goods; read literally it is stock (broth) sold under a trade name, and OXO is the famous British brand of stock cubes.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a brand name for gravy and broth cubes, literally a cooking stock known in commerce by its trademark.

clue.text: Gamble on having a pint to drink with man before night-time

parts.note: ale is beer, a common drink
taken as written
he is the pronoun for a man
after nightfall it is dark

explanation.surface: Someone bets on going to the pub for a pint with a friend before the evening sets in.
explanation.walkthrough: The drink takes the pint after it, then the man and the night-time follow in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A leap in the dark is an idiom for a risky step whose outcome cannot be foreseen, which is a gamble.

clue.text: He may make the earth move

definitions.text: He may make the earth move

parts.note: surface reading: the jokey phrase for a thrilling romantic encounter

parts.words: He may make the earth move
parts.note: setter's reading: a garden designer literally shifts soil about

explanation.walkthrough: 'Did the earth move for you?' is a stock joke about lovemaking; here the earth is shifted with spades and diggers.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden designer reshapes ground, digging and moving soil to remodel the terrain of a plot.

clue.text: Passionately desire to seize day at start of year

indicators.note: to seize something is to grab hold of it, so the word for desire closes round the day

parts.note: will is wish or desire
D is the abbreviation for day

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of year

explanation.surface: Someone longs to seize the day at the beginning of a new year, full of resolutions.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something wildly is to do it with unrestrained feeling, which is what passionately describes.

clue.text: Go silent as one very quietly interrupts, becoming overemotional

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so these letters go inside

parts.note: an actor who dries forgets their lines and falls silent
I is the Roman numeral one
pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very quiet

explanation.surface: Someone falls silent as another softly breaks in, and the conversation turns tearful.
explanation.walkthrough: To dry is theatre slang for forgetting one's lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Drippy is informal for sentimental and feeble, gushing with excessive feeling.

clue.text: Sound of confusion some time in the week

indicators.note: the sound of a word is what is heard when it is spoken, not how it is spelt

parts.note: a daze is a state of confusion

explanation.surface: Someone hears a muddled noise one weekday.
explanation.definitionFit: A week is made up of seven days, so a few of them make up some time within it.

clue.text: See 3
Unhappy acceptance of original order, as decided in advance

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so the word for unhappy holds the rearranged letters

parts.note: pained means distressed or unhappy

indicators.note: done in an original way means arranged afresh, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone grudgingly accepts the original instructions, as was settled beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Original order' looks like a single phrase about first instructions, but 'original' is the signal to rearrange the following word.
explanation.definitionFit: Preordained means fixed or determined beforehand, as by fate, so it matches decided in advance.

clue.text: Fresh way to add salts?

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner
old salts are sailors, and RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A cook asks about a new method of adding salt to food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salts' suggests chemistry or seasoning; an old salt is a sailor, giving RN, the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something modern is new and up to date, which is one sense of fresh.

clue.text: Starter kits

parts.note: surface reading: beginners' packs of equipment for a hobby
setter's reading: the starter is a newborn baby, starting out in life

explanation.walkthrough: A starter kit sounds like a hobby pack; here the starter is a new baby, and the kit is its first wardrobe.
explanation.definitionFit: A layette is the full set of clothes, bedding and linen prepared for a newborn infant.

clue.text: Suggestions also in confusion among supporters

indicators.note: something among others sits in their midst, so it goes inside

parts.note: props are supports that hold something up

indicators.note: letters in confusion are thrown into disorder and must be sorted again

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fans in disarray also throw out ideas of their own.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal is a plan or idea put forward for consideration, so the plural matches suggestions.

clue.text: Hard for engineers to follow code? Not so much

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
Morse is the dot-and-dash telegraph code
less means a smaller amount

explanation.surface: Programmers find a piece of code hard to follow, but perhaps not so very hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorseless means pitiless and relentless, describing someone hard-hearted.

clue.text: Unreliable hearsay a hospital dismissed for ages

indicators.note: an unreliable account cannot be trusted to keep its order, so the letters are rearranged
whatever is dismissed is sent away, so those letters leave the word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
H is the map symbol for a hospital

explanation.surface: Untrustworthy gossip kept a hospital from acting for a very long time.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A and H from the gossip word, then rearrange the five letters that remain.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages is an informal way of saying a long time, as is years in 'I haven't seen her in years'.

clue.text: Draw woman's dislocated elbow up to me

parts.note: Di's, belonging to a woman called Di

indicators.note: in a down answer, going up means reading from bottom to top, so the word is turned round
a dislocated joint is knocked out of place, so these letters are moved around

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman with a dislocated elbow reaches up to draw something close to the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' suggests sketching or pulling; the old sense is to remove the entrails, as in 'hanged, drawn and quartered'.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a carcass or a condemned prisoner was to take out the entrails, which is to disembowel.

clue.text: Army headmaster has diary problem

indicators.note: a problem throws things into disorder, so the letters are mixed up
the head of a word is its opening letter, so just that one is used

parts.note: the head of master is its opening letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A military school's headmaster has trouble with his appointment book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Army headmaster' reads as one phrase, but Army is the definition and only the head of master is used.
explanation.definitionFit: An army can mean any vast number, as in an army of ants, which is what a myriad is.

clue.text: Get Proust for novel free from corruption

indicators.note: something novel is new, so these letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pick up a Proust novel and be spiritually cleansed.
explanation.walkthrough: Proust suggests reaching for a novel; 'novel' is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Rust is the corrosion that eats metal, so a rustproof thing cannot be corroded or decay that way.

clue.text: Bug detected when spies captured scoundrel

indicators.note: the spies hold their captive inside, so the other word goes within

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency
a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A listening device is found after secret agents seize a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' looks like a hidden microphone, which suits the spies; it is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicada is a loud-chirping insect, and bug is a general word for an insect.

clue.text: Back half of the Bull established as kind of brown

indicators.note: keeping only the back half means the front half of the word is dropped

parts.note: Taurus is the zodiac sign of the Bull
set means fixed or established

explanation.surface: The rear end of a bull is plainly a shade of brown.
explanation.definitionFit: Russet is a reddish-brown colour, the shade of autumn leaves and some apples.

clue.text: Consider repairing knocker missing its front

indicators.note: repairing means putting together again, so the letters are reassembled in a new order
a word missing its front has lost its opening letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Think about fixing a door knocker that has lost its front plate.
explanation.definitionFit: To reckon is to judge or regard something in a certain way, which is to consider it.

clue.text: Coming out is difficult to understand

indicators.note: out can mean out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's announcement about coming out is hard to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnomic describes terse, cryptic sayings, pithy but obscure in meaning.

clue.text: Having banned uploads incorrectly, point to major increases

indicators.note: letters set out incorrectly are in the wrong order and need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A website that has wrongly banned uploads points to a jump in its traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass point joins the two words before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: By leaps and bounds is an idiom for rapid, large-scale progress or growth.

clue.text: See 21
Agreement that there's no alternative to higher education

parts.note: uni is short for university

indicators.note: an alternative is another version, so the letters are put in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Everyone agrees that university is the only path after school.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is an alliance or accord between parties, so it can mean an agreement.

clue.text: Quartet finds nothing in hair

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: fur is an animal's hair
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A string quartet finds nothing in its hair — perhaps after a search for lice.
explanation.definitionFit: A quartet is a group of four, so the number names it.

clue.text: Tremendous bottle shown by tedious chap turning up with nothing in tight spot

indicators.note: one thing in another goes inside it

parts.note: a jam is a predicament

indicators.note: a chap turning up is turned head over heels, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a bore is a dull person
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A dull guest arrives at a cramped party bearing an enormous bottle of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeroboam is an oversized wine or champagne bottle, holding several standard bottles.

clue.text: At the same time as beginner disrupts card game

indicators.note: something that disrupts breaks into the middle of an activity, so it goes inside

parts.note: whist is a trick-taking card game
L for learner, a beginner

explanation.surface: A novice spoils the card evening just as everyone sits down to play.
explanation.definitionFit: Whilst is a conjunction meaning during the time that, the same as while.

clue.text: House above offers glimpse of what's at Land's End

indicators.note: a glimpse shows only part of something, here a run of letters inside the words

parts.note: the letters span the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A clifftop house gives a peek of the view at England's tip.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the westernmost point of mainland England, in Cornwall, where the land meets the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: At the very end of the land lies the ocean, so the answer is what is found there.

clue.text: Request a fork's put out

indicators.note: put out means displaced, so the letters are moved around

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A diner asks for a fork to be laid out on the table.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask for something is to make a request for it, a verb phrase equivalent.

clue.text: It helps to plan, when getting vehicle without a loan

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the vehicle sits around the other letters

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
taken as written
a lend is informal for a loan

explanation.surface: Planning helps when you buy a car without borrowing money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside, wrapping the car round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A calendar is a chart of days and months used to schedule appointments and events.
